web/composer/tools/sources.py:R5:_execut: R5 on `if isinstance(resolved, ToolResult): return resolved`. The value is Tier-1/2 server-constructed data, not parsed external input: `resolved` is the return of `_resolve_source_blob`, whose annotation is the owned union `_ResolvedSourceBlob | ToolResult` -- both frozen slotted dataclasses ELSPETH declares. The Tier-3 argument boundary for this tool is upstream and separate: `SetSourceFromBlobArgumentsModel.model_validate` raises `ToolArgumentError` on a malformed payload before `_resolve_source_blob` is ever called. So this is the errors-as-return-values union dispatch ADR-032 prescribes -- `isinstance` against a concrete class we define -- and not a shape guard over foreign data or a swallowed contract violation. It is deliberately NOT narrowed to the house exact-type idiom `type(resolved) is ToolResult`, for two independently sufficient reasons. (1) mypy gives `type(x) is C` NO negative-branch narrowing on this union: measured, the `isinstance` form narrows the negative arm to `_ResolvedSourceBlob` while the exact-type form leaves it as the full `_ResolvedSourceBlob | ToolResult`, which re-types the three following reads -- `resolved.plugin`, `resolved.options` and `resolved.payload` -- back to the bare union and destroys the static proof that the success arm is a `_ResolvedSourceBlob`. Trading real type checking for a lint-shape change would hide more than it reveals. (2) `ToolResult` is deliberately subclassed by test doubles that ride the real compose loop -- `_StrayToolResult` in tests/property/web/composer/test_compose_loop_invariants.py and tests/integration/pipeline/test_composer_llm_eval_characterization.py, `_NonCanonicalizableResult` in tests/unit/web/composer/test_compose_loop_audit_wiring.py -- so an exact-type test would route a genuine `ToolResult` subclass down the success arm. What the check protects: the blob-resolution failure arm. When resolution fails, `_resolve_source_blob` returns a populated rejection `ToolResult` and this branch returns it unchanged, so the failure reaches the planner as a repairable tool failure; falling through instead would construct a `SourceSpec` from a `ToolResult`, which carries no `plugin` or `options`. A `@trust_boundary` is not the right instrument here and would be a false external-source claim -- the file's three honest boundaries all declare `source_param='options'` over composer/LLM-authored option mappings, which is a different value with a different provenance. Invalidated if `_resolve_source_blob` gains a third return variant, or is refactored to a tagged result whose success/error discriminant is read as an explicit field.

The value is Tier-2 validated data, already past the Tier-3 argument boundary: `_execute_upsert_queue_node` takes a `_UpsertNodeArgumentsModel` that `_validate_mutation_arguments` produced by calling `model_validate` on that model (raising `ToolArgumentError` on failure), and its sole caller `_execute_upsert_node` passes `validated.model_copy(update={'options': ...})`, which replaces only `options` and leaves the validated `branches` object untouched. This is normalization of a validated union, not a defensive shape guard hiding a contract violation. It must NOT be narrowed to the house exact-type idiom `type(validated.branches) is dict`, and the reason is a silent data-corruption path rather than a style preference: the else-branch is `tuple(...)`, which applied to a mapping yields a tuple of its KEYS, so under an exact-type test any `Mapping` carrier that is not exactly `dict` would convert a NAMED coalesce branch map into a POSITIONAL branch tuple, succeed, and persist -- destroying branch identity with no error for the author to repair against.
